and the Cursor host features that pstack's skills call by name. The skills ship as upstream wrote them. A small extension supplies the host features in Pi: /name skill commands, Custom Modes, the Task subagent tool, TodoWrite, AskQuestion, the always-applied model rule, /loop, and a system-prompt map from Cursor paths to Pi paths.\nGet set up\n1. Clone the repository and install the package from the checkout. Pi loads a local package in place, so keep the checkout where it is. \ngit clone https://github.com/just-joshn/pi-customizations.git\n \ncd pi-customizations\n \nbun install\n \npi install ./extensions/pi-pstack\n Pi does not install dependencies for a local package, so bun install (or npm install in extensions/pi-pstack) fetches the one runtime dependency, @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime, which only readonly subagents load for their read-only shell. Without it everything else works, and a readonly subagent's shell commands fail instead of running unsandboxed. To try it for one session without installing, run pi -e ./extensions/pi-pstack.\n Installing changes nothing until you invoke a skill. 51 pstack skills stay out of the model's automatic skill list, as in Cursor; only \n/setup-pstack, create-skill, and the three cursor-team-kit skills can load from your words alone.\n2. Run /setup-pstack. It lists the models the Task tool can use, asks for a reasoning budget, maps a model to each role, and writes the model rule. A new rule applies from the next request.\n3. Start real work with /poteto-mode, a goal, and a check that can pass or fail.\nRemove the package with pi remove ./extensions/pi-pstack. Its state lives in ~/.pi/agent/pstack/ (or $PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/pstack/): the model rule, plus one folder per workspace under workspaces/ with subagent transcripts and agent stores. Delete that directory to remove the state too.\nUse it\nYou type\nWhat happens\n/poteto-mode <task>\nThe skill attaches to that one message, as Enter does in Cursor. Every skill Pi loaded works this way, as in Cursor: pstack's (/how, /why, /arena, /interrogate, /principle-prove-it-works, /deslop) and your own, such as a /<handle>-mode skill from /automate-me. /skill:<name> works too.\n/mode poteto-mode [task]\nKeeps the skill in context on every turn, as Option+Enter (Custom Mode) does in Cursor. The footer shows a badge with the skill's Cursor icon and color, such as a yellow ♛ mode: poteto-mode (other skills get the default ⚡). /mode off exits and /mode reports. Any loaded skill can back a mode, including a personal -mode skill from /automate-me.\n/loop 30m <prompt>\nRuns the prompt now and again 30 minutes after each run settles. Without an interval the agent picks each wake with the Loop tool, and the loop ends when it picks none and no background subagent is still running. /loop stop or Escape during a run ends it. The prompt can be a skill or template command, such as /loop 1h /poteto-mode run the audit tick. When a playbook says to arm /loop, the agent starts the loop itself with the Loop tool. Intervals go up to 24 days. Print and JSON runs, including subagents, exit when they settle, so they have no Loop tool and the system prompt tells the agent to keep working instead.\n/setup-pstack\nConfigures the per-role models.\n/poteto-help <question>\nAnswers a question about pstack and hands you a prompt to send.\n/mode and /loop need an interactive or RPC session. This works in interactive, print, JSON, and RPC modes.\nCustom Mode\n/mode <skill> adds the skill to the system prompt on every request, led by poteto-mode's reminder line.\nTask with subagent_type, model, run_in_background, resume, readonly\nTask starts a separate pi --mode json process per subagent. Foreground calls return the response and an agent ID. Background calls return at once, and a <task> notification arrives after your turn ends. One-shot print and JSON runs wait for pending notifications before exiting. Several calls in one message run in parallel. A subagent's own subagents cannot spawn more, and a resumed agent never runs shallower than it was created or than its caller allows. One agent ID never has two running writers, even across Pi processes. Children inherit the parent's project-trust decision (--approve or --no-approve), so they load the same project resources. Foreground usage, including the child's own subagents and compactions, counts toward the session totals. Each child records its own usage in its transcript, and the Task card names the agent type and the model that ran, as Cursor's task card does.\npoteto-agent, comment-sicko\nRead from agents/*.md; the type is the file's name, so pstack 0.15.20's comment-sicko replaces the earlier Comment Sicko. poteto-agent is a delegate that runs in the background by default; the chat that receives /poteto-mode runs the playbook.
